items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: So Roy Eldridge, Dizzy Gillespie, all of the bunch there playing on a Sunday, and they were jamming.

ctx.x: Oh, he could play some beautiful chords. I [bought] -- when I left Philadelphia -- see, we go up to New York and visit. Came up wanted to visit a girlfriend of mine, and so -- okay, this place called a Hut. (Louis Metcalf had a (unintelligible) place on 145th Street where we all used to jam. So I called Louis (unintelligible), said, come on, Hap, says, glad to see you, because we were both writing for the Music Dial. And I said, Billy, let's go down

Billy always carried his horn with him. He would never go anywhere without that horn. I said, look here, I said, 'I'm not going to take my horn,' I said. 'Let's go over and have some fun with the guys.' So Roy Eldridge, Dizzy Gillespie, all of the bunch there playing on a Sunday, and they were jamming. So Billy was concerned -- (unintelligible) said, hey, Hap, he said. Hey, what are you doing, I said. Want you to introduce to a friend of mine, Billy Douglas. Yes, he said, he knows Billy because Billy worked at…

So right then Billy, said, (unintelligible) you got your horn, said, come on and sit in. Well, they're playing them -- [nice] tempo, you know. Said, well, Roy didn't know that this boy had good execution, see, and he run all them chords. See, he got that -- (unintelligible) Benny got it from him.
